newsitem.title: USA: Officials alarmed by extremist groups in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: Officials alarmed by extremist groups in Kansas.

text.p: A recent increase in activity by right-wing anti-government groups prompted Kansas law officials Monday to sound the alarm about the threat of financial fraud and possible violence.

"Never before have the hate groups been so numerous, nor have they been so heavily armed," Sgt. J. D. Mauch, head of the Shawnee County Sheriff Department's Criminal Intelligence Division, told a news conference.

Mauch, whose division has been investigating activities by right-wing groups for two years, said members of the Freemen organisation, which was involved in a lengthy stand-off with the Federal Bureau of Investigation last year in Montana, have recently appeared in Kansas.

Suzanne James, a spokeswoman for the Shawnee County District Attorney's Office, also noted the recent formation in Topeka of a church affiliated with the Chrisian Identity, a white supremacist group that she said has been linked to racial violence in other parts of the country.
"We've got an interesting blend here of political ideology and criminal conduct," James said. "These people are indeed capable of criminal acts."
Mauch said that besides stockpiling weapons and threatening to arrest and try public officials, some groups were operating financial scams aimed at defrauding the government or local banks.

Those schemes include printing bogus checks that appear to be drawn against the U.S. Treasury, and declaring liens against property owned by public officials, creditors or anyone else with whom they have grievances.

Mauch said that although most people in Kansas pay no attention to the bogus checks or the liens, those items often cause headaches to foreign corporations and banks that may not be aware of the groups' strategy.
